wave-20.title: SLICEMATE: Accurate and Scalable Static Program Slicing via LLM-Powered Agents
wave-20.rationale: Re-verification of Wave-19 W1: Yunbo Lyu's homepage lists PTMware at ISSTA 2026, but SliceMate itself is published at ISSTA 2025 (PACMSE Vol 2, ISSTA:2362-2383). ISSTA is not in section 7 whitelist (NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR/FSE/ESEC/ASE/TOSEM/TSE). Mechanism concrete (three LLM agents replace explicit PDG/SDG construction; 22% acc / 28% F1 improvement on SliceBench 2,200-program benchmark) and high-relevance for Wave-20 focus area (b) program-comprehension-mechanism. Watchlist for FSE 2027 / TOSEM 2026 companion paper at an in-list venue. Promoted from Wave-19 W1 (UNVERIFIED) to Wave-20 R1 (REJECT Q1) on 2026-09-07 after venue re-verification.

wave-20.title: Environment-in-the-Loop: Rethinking Code Migration with LLM-based Agents
wave-20.rationale: ReCode 2026 is the 1st International Workshop on Code Translation, Transformation, and Modernization co-located with ICSE 2026; workshop-track. Section 7 workshop-track ACCEPT rationale requires main-track alternative be unavailable; MAgHARCM already anchors the environment-in-the-loop substrate via P-145 TerraMod (ICSE 2026 NIER, main-track subvenue) and existing PRIM-1/22 substrate, so this paper is redundant. Mechanism (semantic code-error feedback guiding LLM agents during migration) concrete but redundant. Watchlist for ICSE 2027 main-track version.

wave-21.title: ABC: Adaptive Bayesian Compression for LLM KV Cache Eviction
wave-21.rationale: February 2026 arXiv preprint only; no peer-reviewed venue confirmation at NeurIPS 2026 / ICML 2026 / ICLR 2026 / FSE 2026 / ICSE 2026 / ASE 2026 / TOSEM 2026 / TSE 2026. The earlier sprint's "Wang et al. ICSE 2026" attribution is a hallucination from a prior iteration; this is the standing-record confirmation that the paper is arXiv-only. Mechanism (Bayesian posterior over KV importance) is concrete but cannot pass Q1 without peer-reviewed venue. Watchlist for ICML 2026 / NeurIPS 2026 / ICLR 2027 companion paper.

wave-21.title: Speculative Actions: Lossless Agentic Acceleration
wave-21.rationale: ICLR 2026 poster using faster models to predict future actions (web search, gaming) and execute them in parallel, committing only when verified. Mechanism is concrete and at an in-list venue, but the speculative-action substrate overlaps substantially with P-137 SuffixDecoding (model-free suffix-tree draft) and the broader P-134/P-137/P-141 speculative-decoding x KV-cache cluster already anchored in PRIM-21/31. No new primitive or mechanism gap is closed. Watchlist for FSE 2027 agentic-comprehension companion paper.

wave-22.title: Code vs. Serialized AST Inputs for LLM-Based Code Summarization: An Empirical Study
wave-22.rationale: LLM4Code is a workshop co-located with ICSE 2026, not the ICSE 2026 main track. Section 7 trigger-list permits workshop-track ACCEPT only for method-level single-paper mechanism work; this paper is an empirical comparison study, not a method-level mechanism. Off-list per section 7.

wave-22.title: SmartComment: Detecting Code-Comment Inconsistencies in Smart Contracts by Combining LLM and Program Analysis
wave-22.rationale: FSE 2026 venue confirmed (in-list), mechanism concrete (LLM-driven review/developer-simulator workflow + comment-propagation/code-context extraction + program-variant differential analysis; 79.9% precision, 81.3% F1 on 1000 real-world smart contracts), but the target domain is Solidity smart contracts, explicitly off-axis from the MAgHARCM modernization substrate (C / Go / Java -> Rust). The four-benchmark target list does not include Solidity.

wave-22.title: Beyond Accuracy: Characterizing Code Comprehension Capabilities in (Large) Language Models
wave-22.verdict: Q1 (off-list workshop venue, diagnostic-framework not mechanism)
wave-22.rationale: DeepTest 2026 is a workshop co-located with ICSE 2026, not the ICSE 2026 main track. The paper proposes a diagnostic framework (binary I/O consistency task + shadow models) rather than a method-level mechanism for code comprehension itself. Diagnostic frameworks are evaluation tools, not method-level mechanisms in the section 7 sense.
